solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Desert, half of area consumed by cratered rock (6)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: the rock swallows the letters, so they end up inside it

blocks.note: the Moon is a rock covered in craters
the first two of AREA's four letters

annotation.surface: A desert landscape, some of it swallowed up by pitted rock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as the noun of sand and dunes, but the definition is the verb: to abandon someone.
annotation.definitionFit: Pirates would abandon a sailor on an empty island, leaving him stranded there, which is deserting him.

entries.clue: Police vehicle with standard outside as well as air-conditioning (5,3)

indicatorNotes.outside: the standard sits outside, wrapping round the other pieces

blocks.note: par is the standard score or level

annotation.surface: A police car fitted with standard trim and air-conditioning.
annotation.walkthrough: The standard wraps round both of the other pieces, not just one.
annotation.definitionFit: The British name for a small patrol car, from the black-and-white or blue-and-white livery the first ones wore.

entries.clue: A tool allowing writer to get to the point? (6-9)

annotation.definition: A tool allowing writer to get to the point?

blocks.note: the writer is not an author but the thing that writes: a pencil
not being concise, but literally acquiring a sharp tip

annotation.surface: An aid for a rambling author who never gets to the point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get to the point' is the stock phrase for cutting the waffle; here the point is the pencil's tip.
annotation.definitionFit: The little bladed device grinds wood away from a blunt lead until the pencil tapers to a fine tip again.

entries.clue: Swine cleaner? Poppycock! (7)

blocks.note: a wash is a cleaning liquid, as in mouthwash or face wash

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a product for cleaning pigs.
annotation.walkthrough: The word was originally kitchen swill fed to pigs, which is how it came to mean worthless talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations dismissing what someone just said as worthless nonsense.

entries.clue: Off and on, all that has come and gone? (5,3,3,4)

annotation.definition2: all that has come and gone?

blocks.clueFragment: all that has come and gone?
blocks.note: read word by word: every 'now' (the present) and every 'then' (the past)

annotation.surface: A wistful look back at everything that has passed, now and again.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a playful literal reading of the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally; taken literally it covers every present moment and every past one, which is everything that has happened.

entries.clue: Make a respectful gesture and amaze dog (3-3)

blocks.note: to wow an audience is to amaze it

annotation.surface: A dog that bows politely and dazzles its audience, as at a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' does double duty in the surface but is only the join between the two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Nursery talk for a pet hound, copied from the sound of its bark.

entries.clue: Young female horse hasn’t finished charge (4)

indicatorNotes.hasn’t finished: the word stops short, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: a filly is a young mare

annotation.surface: A young mare that hasn't completed her charge down the course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge' pretends to be a horse's gallop; here it is the verb as in 'charge your glasses'.
annotation.definitionFit: Charging glasses or a battery means loading them up to capacity, as a toast-master urges before a toast.

entries.clue: Slump, a myth (4)

annotation.surface: A terse claim that some economic slump is only a myth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slump' reads as an economic downturn; it is just the verb to droop.
annotation.definitionFit: The Norse sagas are long legendary tales of heroes and gods, the stuff of mythology.

entries.clue: I doubled energy? (3)

indicatorNotes.doubled: energy is to be used twice, in two different forms

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

annotation.surface: Someone boasts of having doubled their energy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I' reads as the speaker, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin for the first-person pronoun, and the psychologist's term for a person's conscious self.

entries.clue: Fiddle reversing 0-0-4? (6)

indicatorNotes.reversing: the assembled letters are turned round

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O

annotation.surface: A fiddled result: someone reverses a 0-0-4 scoreline.
annotation.walkthrough: The two zeros are read differently, once as a word and once as a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Folk musicians call the four-stringed bowed instrument a fiddle; it is the same instrument.

entries.clue: Scandinavian entry in lexicon, or dictionary (6)

indicatorNotes.entry in: the answer has entered, and sits inside, the words that follow

annotation.surface: Looking up a Scandinavian word in a lexicon or dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Entry' suggests a dictionary headword, which fits the surface; it is really the letters that have entered the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Describes the peoples and countries of northern Europe: Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and their neighbours.

entries.clue: Transformed individual, for many, used to be philanderer (8)

blocks.note: the plural past of 'to be': one was, many were

annotation.surface: A reformed character who, many say, was once a womaniser.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' suggests a man who has changed his ways.
annotation.definitionFit: In folklore a man who changes shape into a wild beast under the full moon.

entries.clue: Snack served with cut of beef, a lip-smacking hit? (7,8)

blocks.note: knuckle is a joint of meat from the leg

annotation.surface: A delicious snack with beef, a real lip-smacking hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lip-smacking hit' sounds like a tasty success; it is a punch that smacks the lips.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for a punch in the mouth, the fist being served up to the face like food.

entries.clue: Hint character heard (3)

indicatorNotes.heard: we want the word that sounds like the letter, not the letter itself

blocks.note: the letter Q, a character of the alphabet

annotation.walkthrough: A character here is a letter of the alphabet, not a person in a play.
annotation.definitionFit: An actor's prompt to speak, or any signal suggesting what to do next.

entries.clue: Strait-laced chief occupies filthy home (7)

indicatorNotes.occupies: the chief moves into, and so sits inside, the home

annotation.surface: A prim boss who has moved into a squalid house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chief' looks like a noun, a boss; it is the adjective, as in arch-villain.
annotation.definitionFit: Stiff and prim in manner, like a collar stiffened with laundry starch.

entries.clue: Greek character taking odd bits from teacup (3)

indicatorNotes.odd bits from: take the letters in odd positions: first, third, fifth

annotation.surface: A Greek man drinking bits of tea from his cup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' here is a letter, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: The nineteenth letter of the alphabet used in Athens, equivalent to our T.

entries.clue: Defender, one crying after Salah’s header (7)

indicatorNotes.header: a header is the top, so the first letter
indicatorNotes.after: the crying one is placed after the S

annotation.surface: A defender in tears after Mohamed Salah scores with a header.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is football throughout: Salah is Liverpool's Egyptian forward and a header is a goal from the head.
annotation.definitionFit: In football, the free defensive player who roams behind the back line clearing up loose balls.

entries.clue: Fine and delicate English article, true (8)

annotation.surface: A dealer's description of a fine, delicate English antique that is genuine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests an object for sale; it is the grammatical word THE.
annotation.definitionFit: So light and airy it seems not of this world, like the ether of the heavens.

entries.clue: Gift posted earlier (7)

annotation.surface: A gift that was put in the mail early.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the opposite order to the clue: earlier, then posted.
annotation.definitionFit: Something handed over free on a birthday or holiday, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Song given smashing analysis (6-9)

blocks.note: a musical number is a song

annotation.surface: A critic calls a song's analysis smashing, meaning excellent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' is British slang for excellent, which is how the surface reads; the wordplay wants the literal breaking sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal term for processing large amounts of data or doing heavy statistical calculation.

entries.clue: Fire jacket (6)

blocks.note: a smart jacket, often in school or club colours

annotation.surface: A fire jacket, as a firefighter might wear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the two words as one fireproof garment; they are separate meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Anything that blazes brightly can be called one, and it is also the club or school jacket, named for the bright colours of the first ones.

entries.clue: Arrested one getting hammered and extremely excited (6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the word's extremes, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone arrested while drunk and highly worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' is British slang for very drunk, which suits the arrest; here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Police slang for catching a suspect and pinning the crime on them.

entries.clue: Rogues, wild animals reportedly? (8)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: the word is as reported, that is, spoken

annotation.surface: Calling a gang of rogues a pack of wild animals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild animals' reads as an insult for the rogues; really it is a species.
annotation.definitionFit: Swindlers and frauds who break rules for gain are dishonest scoundrels.

entries.clue: Loser to tortoise – in race? (4)

blocks.note: the slowest creature there is somehow beat someone
the famous race of Aesop's fable

annotation.surface: Who lost to the tortoise in the famous race?
annotation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable the speedy favourite naps mid-race and the plodding tortoise overtakes.
annotation.definitionFit: The fast, boastful animal in Aesop's fable, beaten because it stopped for a sleep.

entries.clue: Excavate ditch the wrong way, boring (6)

blocks.note: a rut is a furrow or trench

annotation.surface: Someone digging a trench the wrong way round, a tedious job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' fits the digging surface as drilling; it is the definition in its dull sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Pompous, swollen prose that drags on tediously, originally meaning bloated.

entries.clue: French cheese’s picked up for a picnic (6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up by the ear, as speech is

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

annotation.surface: Brie being chosen for a picnic hamper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picnic' is a meal in the surface but means an easy task here, as in 'no picnic'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a task so easy it takes no effort.

entries.clue: Born in due course, last of all (3)

indicatorNotes.last of all: the last letter of every word that precedes it

annotation.surface: A birth that came in due course, the last of all the children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last of all' reads as the youngest child; it asks for the final letter of all three words.
annotation.definitionFit: French for this, placed before a married woman's maiden name.

entries.clue: Noodles, but no starter? So be it! (4)

annotation.surface: A diner resigned to having noodles but no starter course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starter' is a first course of a meal, apt with noodles; here it is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word said at the close of a prayer, meaning let it be so.
